tools.name: maroo_discover
tools.description: Get an adaptive overview of Maroo Network. Call this FIRST in any conversation about Maroo. The response adapts based on what you have already explored — it will suggest different next steps depending on session state.

tools.name: maroo_kb_search
tools.description: Search the Maroo knowledge base (100+ entries). Use this FIRST when you need to understand any Maroo concept, API, or workflow. Returns ranked results with IDs you can pass to maroo_kb_lookup for full content.

tools.name: maroo_kb_lookup
tools.description: Get the full content of a specific knowledge base entry by ID. Use after maroo_kb_search to read complete documentation for a concept, API, or guide.

id.description: Entry ID (from maroo_kb_search results or docs://maroo/ resource URIs)

tools.name: maroo_chain_info
tools.description: Get current Maroo chain status: block height, gas price, network name, RPC URL, and explorer link. Use this to verify chain connectivity or include network context in responses.

tools.name: maroo_wallet_create
tools.description: Create a new Maroo wallet. Generates a random private key and encrypts it with AES-256-GCM at ~/.maroo/keystore/. The passphrase is needed for signing transactions. NEVER share or log the passphrase.

passphrase.description: Encryption passphrase (min 8 chars). Used to encrypt the private key at rest.

tools.name: maroo_wallet_import
tools.description: Import an existing private key into the Maroo keystore. Encrypts with AES-256-GCM. Use this if you already have a wallet from another source.

tools.name: maroo_balance
tools.description: Read the OKRW balance for any Maroo address. When the session has a wallet loaded the `address` argument is optional. Also returns the address's on-chain PCL daily-volume snapshot ({amount, maxAmount, remaining}, the window maroo_pcl_limits reports: maxAmount/remaining null = no daily cap binds the address, e.g. lifted by a KYC attestation; "?" = could not be determined) and the off-chain daily-spending tracker so the caller has the full "how much can I move?" picture in one round trip.

address.description: Address to query (defaults to the session wallet).

tools.name: maroo_preflight
tools.description: Pre-check a transfer BEFORE sending. Validates local policy limits, PCL compliance (the chain's global policy: per-transfer cap, daily volume, KYC attestation), and sufficient balance. ALWAYS call this before maroo_send for Regulated Path transfers. Returns detailed pass/fail for each check with recovery strategies.

tools.name: maroo_pcl_check
tools.description: Compliance preview against the PCL precompile. Evaluates the chain's live global policy for a native OKRW transfer of `value` from `sender` — on testnet: at most 2,000,000 OKRW per transfer and 10,000,000 OKRW per UTC day. A KYC EAS attestation on a regular wallet lifts both caps. For an agent wallet the daily cap is counted per owner (the owners of the agents bound to it) and binds every owner without the attestation. An owner's attestation lifts the per-transfer cap and exempts that owner's own daily counter; the agent wallet's own attestation lifts the per-transfer cap, and exempts a daily counter only when the wallet is itself one of its owners (so a KYC'd agent wallet whose only owner is itself has neither cap) — and returns `allowed` with a reason, the daily `volume` ({amount, maxAmount, remaining, resetAt}) that binds the sender, `perTransferMaxOKRW`, `maxTransferOKRW` (largest transfer allowed right now) and `kycAttested`. In these fields null = the cap does not apply to this sender, "?" = could not be determined (not unlimited). No state changes — pure eth_call reads. Use this before `maroo_send`: the node runs the same check when it receives the transaction, and again before executing it, and refuses a transfer that fails. `maroo_pcl_limits` returns the same limits without a specific amount.

sender.description: Sender address — the wallet whose PCL limits are checked

value.description: OKRW amount as decimal string (e.g. "500" or "0.5")

tools.name: maroo_pcl_limits
tools.description: Read the PCL limits for an address from the chain's live global policy (on testnet: at most 2,000,000 OKRW per transfer and 10,000,000 OKRW per UTC day. A KYC EAS attestation on a regular wallet lifts both caps. For an agent wallet the daily cap is counted per owner (the owners of the agents bound to it) and binds every owner without the attestation. An owner's attestation lifts the per-transfer cap and exempts that owner's own daily counter; the agent wallet's own attestation lifts the per-transfer cap, and exempts a daily counter only when the wallet is itself one of its owners (so a KYC'd agent wallet whose only owner is itself has neither cap)). Returns `{ amount, maxAmount, remaining }` for the daily OKRW volume window that binds the address, as decimal OKRW strings (`amount` = already moved this window, `maxAmount` = cap, `remaining` = headroom), plus `resetAt`/`resetAtIso`, `perTransferMaxOKRW` (single-transfer cap), `maxTransferOKRW` (largest transfer allowed right now), `kycAttested` and `evaluable`. null = the cap does not apply to this address (no need to split a transfer for it); "?" = could not be determined (`evaluable: false`, reasons in `undetermined`) — not unlimited. Use this for "you have N OKRW left until reset" UIs or to plan a transfer split. For "would THIS specific transfer pass?" use `maroo_pcl_check`.

address.description: Address to query (defaults to the session wallet). 40 hex chars, 0x-prefixed.

tools.name: maroo_send
tools.description: Send OKRW to an address. Automatically runs preflight checks (local policy + PCL + balance) as a safety net before signing. Requires wallet passphrase for signing. For Regulated Path transfers, call maroo_preflight first to preview checks. An error with code TX_STATUS_UNKNOWN means the signed transaction may already be pending or mined: check maroo_tx_status with its `txHash` before any resend. TX_FAILED after signing means the node refused it before its mempool (not broadcast); `rejectedBy: "pcl"` means the chain's PCL policy check refused it when the RPC received it.

passphrase.description: Keystore passphrase to decrypt private key for signing

tools.name: maroo_tx_status
tools.description: Get transaction receipt by hash. Returns status (success/reverted), block number, gas used, and logs. Use after maroo_send to confirm a transaction landed. TX_NOT_FOUND means there is no receipt yet. It may still be pending, but the node can accept a transaction and drop it before mining it (PCL is checked when the RPC receives a transaction and again when the pool rechecks it, so a transfer can be dropped if the daily counter or an attestation changes before it is mined), so a TX_NOT_FOUND that lasts may mean it was dropped. TX_NOT_FOUND does not tell a pending transaction from a dropped one, and no maroo tool reads nonces or re-broadcasts a signed transaction. Do not resend while the outcome is unknown: a new maroo_send signs a new transaction, and if this one is still pending both can be mined and move the amount twice. Keep calling maroo_tx_status with this hash, and compare the sender's maroo_balance with its balance before the transfer: a drop by the amount plus gas, with no other transfer in between, means it was mined. Resend only if this hash stays not found and the balance stays unchanged, and only after telling the user that a still-pending copy could also be mined.
